q.t: According to WHO, health is complete well-being in which three areas?
q.e: And not merely the absence of disease.
Bacteria, viruses, fungi, worms, protozoa.

q.t: Diseases that spread from person to person are…
q.e: Typhoid, dengue, flu, TB, malaria.
NCDs don't spread person to person.
Carried by mosquitoes.
It affects the lungs.
Called 'break bone fever'.
They work only against bacterial infections.
From a mould on a petri dish.
Using cowpox material.

q.t: What you FEEL, like pain, is a…
q.e: Symptoms are reported by you.

q.t: What can be SEEN or measured, like fever or rash, is a…
q.e: Signs can be checked by someone else.

o: An insect or animal that carries a pathogen
q.e: The mosquito delivers the protozoan that causes malaria.
Boil water and eat cooked food.

q.t: Common cold and TB spread through…
q.e: Cover your mouth and nose.
Animal bite is its route.
They stop disease before it happens.

o: The body's natural ability to fight disease
q.e: The immune system does it.

q.t: Chronic diseases last more than about…
q.e: Cancer, diabetes, asthma.
Ritucharya is the seasonal routine.

q.t: Why doesn't an antibiotic cure a cold?
o: A cold is viral; antibiotics target bacterial cells
Colds cure themselves only at night
q.e: A virus isn't a cell — nothing for the antibiotic to attack.

o: Resistant bacteria survive and take over
q.e: Vulnerable bacteria die; the few resistant ones multiply.

q.t: Two behaviours that cause antibiotic resistance:
o: Taking them when not needed; not finishing the course
q.e: Use only when prescribed, correct dose, full duration.

q.t: The prevention for each disease always attacks…
q.e: Air → cover mouth; water → boil; vector → stop the insect.

o: It trains the immune system to recognise a germ
q.e: Without you having to catch the disease.

q.t: Why does getting vaccinated protect others too?
o: Fewer infected people means fewer chances to spread
q.e: Community protection.

q.t: Jenner's observation: milkmaids who had cowpox…
q.e: That led to his hypothesis and the first vaccine.

q.t: A student with no friends develops headaches and sleeplessness. Which health failed?
q.e: Nothing infected him — loneliness made him unwell.

q.t: Why do NCDs now cause most deaths in India?
o: More processed food, less exercise, longer lives
q.e: Lifestyle change drives them.
Mosquitoes breed in still water.

q.t: Why did Fleming's accidental discovery happen?
o: He noticed and investigated instead of discarding the dish
q.e: Noticing and investigating made it science.
Caused by lacking specific nutrients.
Harmless parts can train immunity.

o: Scratching skin with smallpox material for mild infection
q.e: Practitioners were called teekedaars.

q.t: Who helped develop the Rotavirus vaccine?
q.e: It protects children from diarrhoea.

q.t: Kamal Ranadive studied links between viruses, hormones and…
q.e: And showed tobacco, diet and pollution raise risk.

q.t: Bhadrak district's sanitation campaign led to…
o: Fewer cases of diarrhoea and infection
q.e: Toilets broke the water-borne route.

q.t: Giving antibiotics to healthy cattle is harmful because…
q.e: Resistance spreads via animals and food.
Worms living as parasites in the intestine.

q.t: 'Prevention is better than cure' is a conclusion because…
o: Avoiding disease is cheaper and easier than treating it
q.e: Clean water, nets, masks and vaccines prevent most diseases here.
